The analysis now fits the meeting it was given. Until now Parley let you choose what to *watch for* but never how to *read* the conversation — every recording came back through the same negotiation lens, laned into "them" and "me", scored on whether you had successfully rebutted the other side, and topped with a section on what you fell short of. That is a fair debrief for a hard negotiation and a strange thing to hand someone after their Tuesday design review.

A recording now has a kind — internal meeting, sales call, price negotiation, or competitor talks — worked out from the transcript when the analysis runs, and changeable from the report page, the findings panel, or the upload wizard if it guessed wrong. The kind decides the shape of everything downstream. An internal meeting produces a record: what got decided, what was left open, and the facts established along the way, followed by a brief with a decisions section, an open-questions section, and a suggested agenda for next time — and no assessment of how you performed, because meeting notes are not a performance review. A sales call is read as an opportunity: the pain the customer described, the objections they raised, and the qualification gaps you left behind. It deliberately does not score you on "winning" an exchange, and an objection you answered still appears as the objection it was. Price negotiations and competitor talks keep the full attack-and-defence read, including which moments you defused.

The built-in template library is now one set per kind, with new watchers written for the two kinds that never had any: an internal meeting is checked for false consensus, work nobody took, scope that grew without anyone weighing it, and blockers left unassigned; a competitor conversation is checked for what you gave away, questions that were fishing rather than negotiating, and commitments you made concretely against a vague answer. The salary-negotiation, job-interview, diligence, general, principled-negotiation and deal-making templates are retired — pick the kind whose read you want instead. Any evaluation set you edited by hand is left alone: a guessed kind will never overwrite a deliberate list.

Two smaller things from the same pass. The titlebar no longer stamps every recording with a "書房" badge and a second "not filed yet" chip — the page tabs beside it already say which mode you are in, and filing belongs to the report page, which is where you notice it needs doing. And action items are now just the thing to do and when it came up; the explanatory line under every one of them doubled the reading for no gain.

For anyone driving Parley over MCP: findings no longer require a `side` and accept a `category` of `decision`, `open`, or `fact`, so an external analyst can write either shape, and the meeting kind is saved alongside the outputs it shaped.
